text.p: The Casablanca stock exchange ended session on Wednesday down 0.53 percent, pressured by declines in blue-chip firms, a market analyst said.
The all-share index closed at 433.81 points, down from 436.12 points on Tuesday.

"The bourse index decline is due an increased volatility in the market and to profit-taking by foreign institutional investors," said Sanae Bennouna, a market analyst at the Casablanca-based Upline Securities.
Upline Securities has an index (USI 10) which tracks the most liquid stocks on the market.
Morocco's largest private ONA Group, closed unchanged at 490 dirhams.
ONA has a market capitalisation of 8.2 billion dirhams.
Societe Nationale d'Investissement, the country's second conglomerate, lost one dirham to close at 558 dirhams.
One of the liquid stocks, Banque Marocaine du Commerce Exterieur lost four dirhams to close at 395 dirhams, a bourse official said.
Fertima fertilser firm, which was recently privatised, was also unchanged at 198 dirhams.
Traded volume on the official market was 48.9 million dirhams compared with 22.1 million dirhams on Tuesday.
